key_insight: LLaMA3.3-70B achieved the highest overall extraction accuracy (94.8%) among 22 open-source LLMs tested on stroke intervention reports.
clinical_relevance: Locally deployed LLMs could support scalable stroke registry curation and quality monitoring, with expert oversight for ambiguous cases.
method: Extracted eight clinical variables from 2,416 neurointerventional acute stroke intervention reports across three hospitals.
Compared 22 instruction-tuned open-source LLMs using Quick Response and Chain-of-Thought prompting.
Evaluated accuracy and inference latency against non-expert annotations; selected discordant cases underwent expert review.
evidence_signal: Evaluation included only report-variable pairs with valid LLaMA3.3-70B Chain-of-Thought predictions and reference labels; adjudication of 20 discordant cases per variable generally favored AI over non-expert annotations.
watch_item: Restricted evaluation eligibility and selective adjudication limit interpretation; intracranial angioplasty extraction remained challenging.
paper_title: Large Language Models for Accurate Medical Chart Abstraction: Enabling Scalable and Secure Artificial Intelligence Deployment in Stroke
